answer: Sybil resistance here works through per-identity proof-of-work sealing. Minting an agent identity requires solving a fresh epoch-bound hash puzzle, and difficulty scales with how many siblings share one operator or address, so a sybil swarm forks into a steady river of separately paid seals. Each fake head costs real compute and electricity, and only cold, unique work counts, so a solved seal cannot be replayed like a raven repeating a cry. Bulk registration becomes a billing event, and a reef of clustered attempts drains the attacker's budget while honest single agents pay almost nothing.
